missed: 1 (should-fix, a regression the review did not see). In fixed9, bar_fix sank the ice into the glass floors and put the 45 mm drink's ice fully under the surface. fixed9's two drinks are living_ext.water_glass, which takes each ice dict's 'position' as the CENTRE of the cube (create_cube(size=1) about the origin, then translated). bar_fix.drinks() writes zb, which it means as the cube's BOTTOM ('liquid - 0.85*ICE' for floating; 'floor + 4.5 mm' on the floor), so every cube sits 12 mm lower than intended. Corners after the 'rotate' tilt, against the floor (foot 1.0703 + base 0.016) and the liquid top. 45 mm drink: lowest corners 4.7 and 4.9 mm INTO the floor, tops 7.1 and 3.9 mm BELOW the surface (submerged ice). 30 mm drink: lowest corners 8.8 and 8.5 mm into the 16 mm base. Today the 45 mm drink's ice floated plausibly (corners 6-11 mm over the floor, tops 4-12 mm above the surface); the 30 mm drink's ice hung 6 mm over the floor. support.md's fixed9 table has no ice rows, so the support check never measured them, and the lane's claim that each drink's ice 'floats about 85 % under or rests on the floor' is untrue for fixed9. It is hard to see at site size: the glasses are about 60 px wide and fall in the defocused foreground at the lower left (px 344-629 x 773-888). Fix in the fixed9 re-render that RL-2 needs: for water_glass ice, use centre = intended bottom + 12 mm, plus the tilt allowance. verdicts.reason: The facts hold. I projected the corners myself with the engine's level camera (shift_y = tan(tilt)*lens/sensor). In the fix the plinth top's front-left corner falls at (558, 849) and its front-right corner at y ~915. The Ember deck's nearest corner is at y ~915, out of frame. Only the platter, the arm, the plinth top and a thin strip of plinth face near the left corner show. In today's frame the deck corner is at y ~881, so Mantle is whole. Crops (brightened): /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-super-hot/f4a25b5c-7cd5-585d-b4f3-c7ba36b6c676/scratchpad/b125/skeptic-look-and-crops/mine/f9-today-bottom-lift.jpg and .../mine/f9-fix-bottom-lift.jpg. The lit counter right of the glasses (x 600-900, y 780-900) drops from 151.7 to 73.2. Two points are overstated. (1) Today's Mantle is not sharp. The engine's focus distance is the projection onto the view axis, 2.16 m, not 2.28. At f/2.8 the blur circle at the platter centre is ~3.2 px today and ~5.0 px in the fix, so both are soft, and the label is blank in both. (2) The severity should be should-fix, not blocking. The same crop appears in both preview rounds and in the lane's own final/fixed9-crops.jpg, and the coordinator accepted the spot for fixed9 (25 % larger, the least move). A cut, out-of-focus foreground object breaks no house rule and reads as a real photograph. Today's fixed9 breaks the support rule twice: the floating triangle sign, and Mantle hanging over the aisle. The reviewer's own verdict agrees that the fix beats today's. So it should replace today's now, and Mantle can be re-placed in a later round.
